18380-the-war-after-the-war.title: After The War
18380-the-war-after-the-war.creator: Unknown
18380-the-war-after-the-war.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. This is why I made two trips to Europe: why I submit this little book in the hope that it may point the way to some realisation of the immense responsibilities which will inevitably crowd upon the world and more especially upon the United States.

arxiv-2106-07980.title: Grounds for Suspicion: Physics-based Early Warnings for Stealthy Attacks on Industrial Control Systems
arxiv-2106-07980.creator: Mazen Azzam, Liliana Pasquale, Gregory Provan, and Bashar Nuseibeh
arxiv-2106-07980.description: Abstract Stealthy attacks on Industrial Control Systems can cause significant damage while evading detection. In this paper, instead of focusing on the detection of stealthy attacks, we aim to provide early warnings to operators, in order to avoid physical damage and preserve in advance data that may serve as an evidence during an investigation.

arxiv-2212-06789.title: Emergent grain boundary phases in stressed polycrystalline thin films
arxiv-2212-06789.creator: Mengyuan Wang, Ruilin Yan, Xiao Han, Hailong Wang, Moneesh Upmanyu
arxiv-2212-06789.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mengyuan Wang, Ruilin Yan, Xiao Han, Hailong Wang, Moneesh Upmanyu. The grain boundary (GB) microstructure influences and is influenced by the development of residual stresses during synthesis of polycrystalline thin films. Recent studies have shown that the frustration between the preferred growth direction and rotations of abutting crystals to local cusps in GB energies leads to internal stresses localized within nanoscopic surface layers around the valleys and ridges that form at emergent boundaries (eGBs).

arxiv-2405-04213.title: On left braces in which every subbrace is an ideal
arxiv-2405-04213.creator: A. Ballester-Bolinches, R. Esteban-Romero, L. A. Kurdachenko, V. Pérez-Calabuig
arxiv-2405-04213.description: Abstract The aim of this paper is to introduce and study the class of all left braces in which every subbrace is an ideal. We call them Dedekind left braces. It is proved that every finite Dedekind left brace is centrally nilpotent.

arxiv-2409-06075.title: DNA sequence alignment: An assignment for OpenMP, MPI, and CUDA/OpenCL Thanks: This work has been developed in the context of the GAMUVa group ( https://gamuva.infor.uva.es/ ), and it has been partially supported by Vicerrectorado de Innovación Docente y Transformación Digital de la Universidad de V
arxiv-2409-06075.creator: Arturo Gonzalez-Escribano, Diego García-Álvarez, Jesús Cámara
arxiv-2409-06075.description: Abstract We present an assignment for a full Parallel Computing course. Since 2017/2018, we have proposed a different problem each academic year to illustrate various methodologies for approaching the same computational problem using different parallel programming models. They are designed to be parallelized using shared-memory programming with OpenMP, distributed-memory programming with MPI, and GPU programming with CUDA or OpenCL.

arxiv-2410-03333.title: Comparative Analysis and Ensemble Enhancement of Leading CNN Architectures for Breast Cancer Classification
arxiv-2410-03333.creator: Gary Murphy, Raghubir Singh
arxiv-2410-03333.description: Abstract This study introduces a novel and accurate approach to breast cancer classification using histopathology images. It systematically compares leading Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models across varying image datasets, identifies their optimal hyperparameters, and ranks them based on classification efficacy.

arxiv-2504-06291.title: Performance optimization of Nernst-based thermionic engines
arxiv-2504-06291.creator: Wei Yan 1, Minglong Lv 1, Ousi Pan 1, Zhimin Yang 2, Jincan Chen 1, Shanhe Su 1
arxiv-2504-06291.description: Abstract In this paper, we examine the power and efficiency of the thermionic device utilizing the Nernst effect, with a specific focus on its potential application as an engine. The device operates by utilizing the vertical heat current to generate a horizontal particle current against the chemical potential.

arxiv-2508-08468.title: Audio–Visual Speech Enhancement: Architectural Design and Deployment Strategies
arxiv-2508-08468.creator: Anis Hamadouche, Haifeng Luo, Mathini Sellathurai and Tharm Ratnarajah
arxiv-2508-08468.description: Abstract This paper introduce a new AI-based Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement (AVSE) and presents a comparative performance analysis of deployment architectures. The proposed AVSE system integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spectral feature extraction and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for temporal modeling, enabling robust speech enhancement through multimodal fusion of audio and visual cues.

arxiv-2511-17282.title: Where Culture Fades: Revealing the Cultural Gap in Text-to-Image Generation
arxiv-2511-17282.creator: Chuancheng Shi, Shangze Li, Shiming Guo, Simiao Xie, Wenhua Wu, Jingtong Dou, [2pt] Chao Wu, Canran Xiao, Cong Wang, Zifeng Cheng, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua, [4pt] The University of Sydney
arxiv-2511-17282.description: Abstract Multilingual text-to-image (T2I) models have advanced rapidly in terms of visual realism and semantic alignment, and are now widely utilized. Yet outputs vary across cultural contexts: because language carries cultural connotations, images synthesized from multilingual prompts should preserve cross-lingual cultural consistency.

arxiv-2512-10741.title: TRIDENT: A Redundant Architecture for Caribbean-Accented Emergency Speech Triage
arxiv-2512-10741.creator: Galbraith, E, Sutherland, C, Morgan, D
arxiv-2512-10741.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Galbraith, E, Sutherland, C, Morgan, D. Emergency speech recognition systems exhibit systematic performance degradation on non-standard English varieties, creating a critical gap in services for Caribbean populations. We present TRIDENT ( T ranscription and R outing I ntelligence for D ispatcher- E mpowered N ational T riage), a three-layer dispatcher-support architecture designed to structure emergency call inputs for human application of established triage protocols (the ESI for routine operations and START for mass casualty events), even when automatic speech recognition fails.

arxiv-2602-18860.title: Frozen and Growing Quantum Work under Noise: Coherence and Correlations as Key Resources
arxiv-2602-18860.creator: Mohammad B. Arjmandi
arxiv-2602-18860.description: Abstract We explore the decomposition of ergotropy into incoherent and coherent parts for quantum systems exposed to typical Markovian noise channels. The incoherent contribution arises from population inversion in the energy eigenbasis after dephasing, while the coherent contribution reflects the impact of quantum coherence on work extraction.

pmc-10635452.title: Therapeutic evaluation and analysis of complications of ethanol sclerotherapy for intramuscular vascular malformations: a single-center retrospective study
pmc-10635452.creator: Cai-Jun Jin, Qian Wang, Min Wang, Yong Chen, Si-Ming Yuan
pmc-10635452.description: BackgroundIntramuscular venous malformations (IMVMs) can cause pain and contracture deformity, leading to dysfunction of limbs. Ethanol sclerotherapy is one of the main treatments for IMVMs. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and the complications associated with intravascular ethanol sclerotherapy for IMVMs and to provide a comprehensive summary of clinical experiences for future reference.

pmc-10675038.title: Ultrasonic Spray Coating to Optimize Performance of Bio-Electrochemical Systems
pmc-10675038.creator: Giacomo Spisni, Giulia Massaglia, Fabrizio C. Pirri, Stefano Bianco, Marzia Quaglio
pmc-10675038.description: This work investigates the optimization of carbon-based electrodes employed in bio-electrochemical systems (BES) through the deposition of nanostructured layers of poly(3,4-ethylene-dioxy-thiophene) poly(styrene-sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) on commercial carbon paper electrodes via ultrasonic spray coating (USC). This innovative application of USC demonstrated that uniform and controlled depositions of PEDOT:PSS can be successfully performed on carbon-based electrodes.

pmc-10976650.title: The role of inflammatory and remodelling biomarkers in patients with non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-10976650.creator: Hemn Abdalla Omer, Christer Janson, Kawa Amin
pmc-10976650.description: IntroductionBiomarkers play a crucial role in evaluating the prognosis, diagnosis, and monitoring of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The aim of this study was to compare the levels of inflammatory and remodelling biomarkers among patients with NSCLC and healthy controls (HCs) and to investigate the correlation between these biomarkers.Material and methodsBlood samples were taken from 93 NSCLC and 84 HCs.

pmc-11311823.title: Functional Characterization of JcSWEET12 and JcSWEET17a from Physic Nut
pmc-11311823.creator: Pingzhi Wu, Youting Wu, Zhu Yu, Huawu Jiang, Guojiang Wu, Yaping Chen
pmc-11311823.description: Physic nut (Jatropha curcas L.) has attracted extensive attention because of its fast growth, easy reproduction, tolerance to barren conditions, and high oil content of seeds. SWEET (Sugar Will Eventually be Exported Transporter) family genes contribute to regulating the distribution of carbohydrates in plants and have great potential in improving yield and stress tolerance.

pmc-11458542.title: Caregiver acceptance of human papillomavirus vaccine for their female children in Chileka, Blantyre, Malawi
pmc-11458542.creator: Akim N Bwanali, Petro Liundi, Adriano F Lubanga, Samuel L Mpinganjira, Luis A Gadama
pmc-11458542.description: Highlights•Cervical cancer poses a major health burden in Malawi.•Vaccination against the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) offers a feasible tool for reducing the burden.•Lack of knowledge on cervical cancer and the HPV vaccine and misconceptions hinder the uptake of the HPV vaccine.•Comprehensive and sustainable awareness programmes should be designed and implemented to address the barriers to HPV vaccination.

pmc-11509529.title: Cyanobacterial Blooms in City Parks: A Case Study Using Zebrafish Embryos for Toxicity Characterization
pmc-11509529.creator: Bruna Vieira, João Amaral, Mário Jorge Pereira, Inês Domingues
pmc-11509529.description: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes that play an important role in the ecology of aquatic ecosystems. However, they can also produce toxins with negative effects on aquatic organisms, wildlife, livestock, domestic animals, and humans. With the increasing global temperatures, urban parks, renowned for their multifaceted contributions to society, have been largely affected by blooms of toxic cyanobacteria.

pmc-11603755.title: Long-read sequencing enables comprehensive molecular genetic diagnosis of Fabry disease
pmc-11603755.creator: Fengxia Yao, Na Hao, Danhua Li, Weimin Zhang, Jingwen Zhou, Zhengqing Qiu, Aiping Mao, Wanli Meng, Juntao Liu
pmc-11603755.description: BackgroundThe clinical diagnosis of Fabry Disease (FD) can be challenging due to the clinical heterogeneity, especially in females. Patients with FD often experience a prolonged interval between the onset of symptoms and receiving a diagnosis. Genetic testing is the gold standard for precise diagnosis of FD, however conventional genetic testing could miss deep intronic variants and large deletions or duplications.

pmc-12538306.title: Acquired Venous Malformation of Bilateral Upper Eyelids
pmc-12538306.creator: Airi Kimura, Yuki Mizutani, Keiichi Yamanaka
pmc-12538306.description: An elderly female presented with a two‐year history of bilateral erythematous swellings on the upper eyelids. Doppler ultrasonography demonstrated a low‐flow vascular pattern. Skin biopsy revealed vascular hyperplasia characterized by slit‐like irregular vessels. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of acquired venous malformation of the bilateral upper eyelids was established.

pmc-13371917.title: The earliest amber from the Middle Devonian of China
pmc-13371917.creator: Cihang Luo, Huiyuan Yang, Honghe Xu, Zixiao Yang, Shengyu Wang, Michael S. Engel, Bingcai Liu, Edmund A. Jarzembowski, Brendon E. Boudinot, Xingqian Cui, Haichun Zhang, Bo Wang
pmc-13371917.description: Resin production is a major innovation in land plants, signaling the evolution of specialized secretory systems, complex terpenoid biosynthesis, and defensive and wound-sealing functions. Yet its origin remains poorly constrained because fossilized resin (amber) is exceedingly rare in Paleozoic deposits, with the earliest widely accepted amber record from the Late Carboniferous.
